s700_PP_r2: Hello! Use a before a consonant sound (a book) and an before a vowel sound (an apple). Try this one: She has ___ orange in her bag. Write only the missing word.
s706_PP_r2: Hello! Remember: a goes before a consonant sound (a dog), and an goes before a vowel sound (an egg). Here is your first exercise: My uncle is ___ doctor. Write only the missing word.
s712_PP_r2: Hello! We use the for something already mentioned: I have a dog. The dog is brown. Now you try: We have a garden. ___ garden is small. Write a or the.
s718_PP_r2: Hello! We use can + the base verb, like I can swim. Try this one. Correct the sentence: "She can swims."
s724_PP_r2: Hello! After can we use the base verb, with no -s: I can swim, she can cook. Here is your exercise. Correct the sentence: "She can swims."
s730_PP_r2: Hello! Every sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. The word I is always a capital letter too. Try this one. Rewrite correctly: "my brother likes tea"
s736_PP_r2: Hello! Use am with I, is with he, she and it, and are with you, we and they. Try this one: I ___ a student. Write only the missing word.
s742_PP_r2: Hello! Remember: am goes with I, is goes with he, she and it, and are goes with you, we and they. Never leave the word out! Your first exercise: She ___ at home today. Write only the missing word.
s748_PP_r2: Hello! We use at with clock times (at 7 o'clock), on with days (on Monday) and in with months (in July). Try this one. Write in, on or at: My train leaves ___ 5 o'clock.
s754_PP_r2: Hello! We use There is with one thing (There is a table) and There are with more than one (There are two chairs). Try this one. Complete: "___ three windows in my room."
s760_PP_r2: Hello! Use There is for one thing and There are for many things: There is a table. There are two chairs. Here is your first exercise. Complete: "___ a big table in the kitchen."
s766_PP_r2: Hello! In English the order is subject, then verb, then object. Words like usually go before the main verb, and place or time goes at the end: We usually have lunch at one. Try this one. Put in order: "plays / Sam / chess / on Mondays"
s772_PP_r2: Hello! Let's practise classroom words. Here is your first exercise. Complete: "I sit on a ___."
s778_PP_r2: Hello! Let's practise classroom words. Here is your first exercise. Complete: "The teacher writes on the ___."
s784_PP_r2: Hello! Days and months are part of this lesson. We use on with days (on Monday) and in with months (in July). Try this one. Write in, on or at: They get married ___ April.
s790_PP_r2: Hello! Family words are great for this lesson. We say "This is my brother. He is twelve." Try this one. Complete: "This is my grandmother. ___ is very kind."
s796_PP_r2: Hello! Let's practise family words. Use he for a man or boy, and she for a woman or girl. Try this one. Complete: "This is my brother. ___ is twelve."
s802_PP_r2: Hello! Let's practise food and drink words. Here is a riddle. Write the word: you drink it, it is white. ___
s808_PP_r2: Hello! Let's practise rooms in a home. Try this one. Complete: "My bed is in the ___."
s814_PP_r2: Hello! Let's practise rooms in a home and what we do in them. Try this one. Complete: "I make toast in the ___."
s820_PP_r2: Hello! Read this short dialogue. Sara: "Let's meet at half past four." Tom: "Sorry, I can't. Can we meet at quarter to five?" Sara: "Yes, quarter to five is fine." What time do they meet?
s826_PP_r2: Hello! To ask nicely, we say "Can I have ... please?" instead of a blunt command. Try this one. You are thirsty in a cafe. Ask for a tea politely.
s832_PP_r2: Hello! A polite request sounds like this: "Can I have a water, please?" Now you try. Make this polite: "Give me a coffee."
s838_PP_r2: Hello! For short adjectives we add -er (small, smaller than). For long adjectives we use more ... than. Try this one. Complete: "Cairo is ___ (big) than Luxor."
s844_PP_r2: Hello! We use and to add, but to show a difference, and because to give a reason. Try the first one. Join with and: "I have a cat. I have a dog."
s850_PP_r2: Hello! We join short sentences with and, but or because. Let's start with but, which shows a difference. Join with but: "The bus is cheap. It is slow."
s856_PP_r2: Hello! Frequency words like always, usually, sometimes and never go before the main verb, and after he, she or it the verb takes -s. Try this one. Correct the verb: "She go to bed at ten."
s862_PP_r2: Hello! We make plans with am/is/are + going to + base verb: I am going to study tonight. Here is your exercise. Correct: "I going to study tonight."
s868_PP_r2: Hello! For plans we use going to: She is going to visit her aunt. Try this one. Complete: "They ___ (play) football next Saturday." Write the full verb phrase for a plan.
s874_PP_r2: Hello! We use many with things we can count (bottles) and much with things we cannot count (water). Try this one. Write much or many: How ___ bottles are there?
s880_PP_r2: Hello! For past questions we use Did + subject + base verb: Did you watch TV last weekend? Now you try. Make a question with did: "You visited your friend." Start with Did.
s886_PP_r2: Hello! In past questions we use Did and the base verb, not the past form: Did she go to the park? Try this one. Write a question with Did: "He played football on Saturday."
s892_PP_r2: Hello! Some verbs are irregular in the past, like go becomes went and eat becomes ate. Try this one. Write the past form of 'have': Yesterday I ___ a big lunch.
s898_PP_r2: Hello! For many verbs we add -ed to talk about the past: I walked to the park. Try this one. Write the past form of 'play': Last weekend I ___ football with my friends.
s904_PP_r2: Hello! To talk about finished actions, add -ed to the verb: I cleaned my room. Here is your exercise. Write the past form of 'watch': On Saturday we ___ a film.
s910_PP_r2: Hello! We use am/is/are + verb-ing to say what is happening now: The children are playing. Imagine a park. Write two sentences about what people are doing now.
s916_PP_r2: Hello! We use some in positive sentences (I would like some tea) and any in questions and negatives (Do you have any cake?). Try this one. Write some or any: I would like ___ water, please.
s922_PP_r2: Hello! Use some in positive sentences and any in negatives and questions: We don't have any milk. Is there any juice? Try this one. Write some or any: Do you have ___ sandwiches?
s928_PP_r2: Hello! After he, she and it, we add -s to the verb: He plays, she drinks. Try this one. Write the correct form: My sister ___ (play) tennis on Sundays. Answer with only the verb.
s934_PP_r2: Hello! We use has with he, she and it: My cousin has brown eyes. Try this one. Complete: "My cousin ___ brown eyes." Choose has or have.
s940_PP_r2: Hello! Let's describe people. Try this exercise. Write two sentences about a famous actor: one about hair or eyes and one about personality.
s946_PP_r2: Hello! To ask a price we say "How much is this hat?" or "How much are these shoes?" Try this one. Correct this question: "How much cost this hat?"
s952_PP_r2: Hello! Let's match jobs to workplaces. Try this one. Complete: "A chef works in a ___."
s958_PP_r2: Hello! Let's match jobs and workplaces. Remember to use an before a vowel sound. Try this one. Complete: "A pilot works at an ___."
s964_PP_r2: Hello! Let's practise weather words like sunny, rainy, windy and cold. Try this one. Complete: "Take an umbrella. It is ___ today."
s982_PP_r2: Hello! Here is a quick check. Write in, on or at: They get married ___ April. Then tell me one more example of your own using on with a day or date, for example a holiday.
s988_PP_r2: Hello! Here is an exercise. Turn this statement into a past question with did: "She went to the market on Saturday." Then answer it with a short answer, yes or no.
